name: Grist
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace

tiers.name: Cloud Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited documents; 5,000 records/document; 30-day snapshots; 5,000 API calls/document/day; 1 GB attachments/document; 2 free guests/document; 100 AI credits lifetime.

tiers.name: Cloud Pro
tiers.limits: 100,000 records/document; 3-year history; 40,000 API calls/document/day; 3 GB attachments/document; 100 AI credits/month.

tiers.name: Cloud Business
tiers.limits: 150,000 records/document; 5-year history; 60,000 API calls/document/day; 20 GB attachments/document; 2,000 AI credits/month.

tiers.name: Cloud Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom record, API, storage and support limits; enterprise controls; pricing page displays a 50-user minimum.

tiers.name: Self-hosted Community
tiers.limits: Open-source Community edition on the customer's own infrastructure.
tiers.notes: A free activation key is offered to qualifying organizations with less than $1 million in annual revenue plus funding.

tiers.name: Self-hosted Grist
tiers.limits: Paid self-hosted edition with advanced administration, AI, automations and audit features.

tiers.name: Self-hosted Enterprise
tiers.limits: Enterprise self-hosted controls and support; 50-user minimum.

tiers.name: Hosting Services
tiers.limits: Managed hosting and services; public page gives no numeric capacity or price.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Cloud Free: unlimited documents, 5,000 records/document, 30-day snapshots, 5,000 API calls/document/day, 1 GB attachments/document, 2 guests/document and 100 AI credits lifetime; self-hosted Community is also $0 on your infrastructure
pricing.billingTerms: cloud and paid self-hosted plans offer monthly + annual billing; annual prices shown are 20% lower; Enterprise and hosting are quote-based
pricing.hiddenCosts: Cloud Business has a 5-user minimum; Enterprise offerings show a 50-user minimum; only 2 guests/document are free on Cloud; AI add-ons cost $10/month for 500 credits or $29/month for 2,000; self-hosting infrastructure is separate.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Grist, combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace. The hard boundary is mature formula engine, access rules, collaboration, integrations, and hosting, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: mature formula engine, access rules, collaboration, integrations, and hosting
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Grist because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Community
alternatives.desc: A friendlier database grid with relations and formulas; less spreadsheet-like, more app-builder-like.

facts.dataFormat: Rows and application metadata live in the operator's PostgreSQL database; uploads live in the mounted media volume or configured object storage; tables export as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow is less spreadsheet-like and cannot match Grist's Python-powered formulas, computed records, and flexible document-level analysis.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, persistent PostgreSQL and media volumes, secrets, backups, and public-URL/TLS configuration for shared use

alternatives.name: Grist
alternatives.desc: The actual product, self-hosted: formulas, relational records, forms, and views in one small workspace.

facts.install: Hosted signup, desktop app, or Docker container for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Each document is a .grist SQLite database containing table data, attachments, document metadata, and recent history; CSV/Excel exports are also available
facts.gapVsPaid: Self-hosting preserves the product but gives up the paid hosted service's managed upgrades, backups, secure sharing, support, and operational reliability.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted or desktop use; shared self-hosting requires Docker, authentication, backups, a public URL, and safe Python-formula sandboxing

alternatives.name: Teable Community
alternatives.desc: Relational tables, formula fields, forms, and views in a tidy self-hosted grid.

facts.dataFormat: Records and metadata live in PostgreSQL; attachments use local storage or configured S3-compatible object storage; bases can be backed up as .tea files
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable's formula system is much less programmable than Grist's Python formulas and cannot reproduce complex spreadsheet-style computed logic as cleanly.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, PostgreSQL, object-storage/persistent-volume planning, secrets, backups, and at least roughly 4 GB RAM; standalone Community Edition omits cloud AI and App Builder

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mathesar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent relational data editing, but no spreadsheet formula model, the feature that makes Grist Grist.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Grist in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: combine spreadsheet formulas with relational records in a small self-hosted workspace, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
